title: rorca-mcp-reliability
specName: MCP Reliability: Async Substrate + Model Registry + Operational Hardening

userStories.title: Universal async jobs table and enqueue/poll API
userStories.description: Create a `jobs` table and two API endpoints that become the universal substrate for every long-running Rorca operation. Any operation that can take longer than a few seconds — spec generation, enrichment, batch generation, workspace hydration, model probing — must be expressible as a job. POST /api/jobs enqueues a job and returns {jobId, status: 'queued'} in under 200ms. GET /api/jobs/:id returns {jobId, status, progress, result, error, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt}. Status values: queued | running | done | failed. The result field holds the full operation output when done. The error field holds structured failure info when failed: {message, code, retriable}. Jobs are stored in pg-boss (reusing the existing queue infrastructure) under a queue name derived from the job type (e.g. 'jobs:spec-generate', 'jobs:enrich'). The jobs table in pg-boss IS the persistence layer — no separate DB table needed. Write a thin wrapper `backend/src/lib/job-queue.ts` with: enqueueJob(type, payload, opts?) → Promise<{jobId}>, getJobStatus(jobId) → Promise<JobStatus>, and completeJob / failJob helpers used by workers. Include idempotency: enqueueJob accepts an optional idempotencyKey; if a job with that key already exists in a non-failed state, return the existing jobId without re-enqueueing.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/jobs with body {type: 'spec-generate', payload: {...}, idempotencyKey: 'abc'} returns {jobId, status: 'queued'} in < 200ms
GET /api/jobs/:id returns full status object with all fields
Calling POST /api/jobs twice with the same idempotencyKey returns the same jobId both times
Backend type-check passes with no new type errors
job-queue.ts exports: enqueueJob, getJobStatus, completeJob, failJob

userStories.title: Refactor spec generate to return jobId immediately
userStories.description: Rewrite POST /api/specs/generate so it ALWAYS returns {jobId} in < 500ms regardless of story count, multiPass, or any other option. Remove the CHUNK_THRESHOLD branch entirely — there is no longer a synchronous path for generation. The route handler enqueues a 'jobs:spec-generate' pg-boss job with the full generation payload and returns immediately. The actual generation work (including multi-pass, chunking, direction synthesis, OpenCode calls) runs inside the worker that picks up the job. Worker writes progress updates via completeJob/failJob. The existing `spec-gen-chunked.ts` and `multiPass` pipeline become the single implementation path, both executed in the worker. Result payload when done: {specId, specPath, storyCount, generationLog}. Error payload when failed: {message, code: 'GENERATION_FAILED', retriable: true, detail}. Do not change any generation logic — only move execution from the HTTP request handler into the job worker.

POST /api/specs/generate returns {jobId, status: 'queued'} even when multiPass: true
After the worker completes the job, GET /api/jobs/:id returns {status: 'done', result: {specId, specPath, storyCount}}
A 500-story spec request does not cause an HTTP timeout — the client gets jobId immediately
Synchronous CHUNK_THRESHOLD branch removed from specs.ts

userStories.title: Refactor enrich to return jobId immediately with per-story progress
userStories.description: Rewrite POST /api/specs/:specId/enrich so it always returns {jobId} in < 200ms. Enrichment work (all story annotation calls) runs in the worker. Worker updates job progress field after each story batch completes: {storiesTotal, storiesDone, storiesFailed, annotations: [...]}. When all batches finish, worker calls completeJob with {storiesEnriched, storiesFailed: [{storyId, error}], requestedModel, actualModel, substitutionReason}. The substitutionReason field is populated whenever resolveModel() falls back (Phase 2 introduces resolveModel; for now use the existing isValidModel + DEFAULT_MODEL fallback already added to specs.ts). Concurrency cap of 3 stays. The 'failures array' must ALWAYS be present in the result even when empty — consumers must never need to guess whether failures occurred.

userStories.title: Refactor batch spec generation and workspace hydration to use job substrate
userStories.description: Apply the same async refactor to two more long-running routes: (1) POST /api/specs/generate-batch — currently spawns N generation calls synchronously; refactor to enqueue one 'jobs:batch-generate' job per spec in the batch, return {batchId, jobIds[]}. Existing batch tracking in `spec_generation_jobs` table can remain but jobs are now pg-boss backed. (2) POST /api/workspaces/:id/hydrate — LLM map-reduce call can take 5-10 minutes; refactor to enqueue 'jobs:hydrate' and return {jobId}. Both routes must return their job references in < 500ms. This story is deliberately narrow: only the HTTP handler → async handoff changes. All generation/hydration logic stays in the existing functions.

userStories.title: MCP polling wrapper: rorca_job_status tool + async-aware tool wrappers
userStories.description: Add one new MCP tool and update all generation tools to return jobId patterns that Claude can poll. New tool: rorca_job_status(jobId) — calls GET /api/jobs/:id and returns the full status object. Claude uses this after any tool call that returns a jobId to poll until status = 'done' or 'failed'. userStories.title: Error surfacing: structured failures always reach the MCP caller
userStories.description: Today Promise.allSettled swallows errors silently — the caller sees success:true, storiesEnriched:0 with no explanation. Fix: (1) Every job result must include a top-level failures[] array with {operation, error: {message, code}, retriable} entries. (2) Every job failure (status='failed') must include a structured error with code, message, and detail. (3) Add an AppError hierarchy entry: GenerationError (500, code: GENERATION_FAILED), EnrichError (500, code: ENRICH_FAILED), HydrationError (500, code: HYDRATION_FAILED). (4) The rorca_job_status MCP tool must surface failures prominently in its summary string: 'FAILED: 14 stories failed to enrich. Errors: [rate_limit_exceeded x9, invalid_model x5]. Action: check model availability or retry.' (5) Log every failure with structured fields {jobId, operation, storyId, model, errorCode, errorMessage} at warn level so failures are findable in backend logs even without a UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Enriching a spec with an invalid model returns a job result with failures[] listing every story that failed and why
A job with status='failed' always has error.code and error.message (never undefined)

userStories.title: model-registry.ts library with resolveModel and recordRunOutcome
userStories.description: Create backend/src/lib/model-registry.ts with the following exports: (1) resolveModel(requestedId, opts?) → Promise<ResolvedModel | null>: looks up the model in model_capabilities. Returns the model if registered and probe_status != 'unavailable'. Returns null if unknown or unavailable. opts.allowDegraded defaults true. ResolvedModel = {provider, modelId, displayName, probeStatus, recentSuccessCount, health}. (2) listAvailableModels(opts) → Promise<RegisteredModel[]>: filtered by provider, probe_status (default: NOT unavailable), sorted by recent_success_count DESC. (3) recordRunOutcome(provider, modelId, success: boolean): increments recent_success_count or recent_failure_count, updates last_succeeded_at on success, updates updated_at. Called from execution-engine after each story. (4) recordProbeResult(provider, modelId, status, error?, latencyMs?): updates probe fields. Stub for Phase 2 probes. (5) computeHealth(row) → 'healthy' | 'degraded' | 'unavailable': composite scoring. NEVER marks unavailable if recent_success_count (last 7 days) > 5, regardless of probe_status. This protects gpt-5.4 which has 535 successful stories.

userStories.title: Seed registry from existing sources on startup
userStories.description: On backend startup, call seedModelRegistry() which runs idempotently: (1) Read ~/.codex/models_cache.json if present. Upsert models with visibility='list' as provider='codex', requires_subscription=true, probe_status='unknown'. Only update static fields (display_name, context_window) on conflict — never reset metric fields. (2) Read ALL_MODELS from llm-client.ts. Upsert with appropriate provider per model prefix (claude-* → claude, gpt-* → openai, gemini-* → google, etc.). (3) Backfill historical runs: scan DISTINCT (agent_type, agent_model) from pipeline_runs over last 30 days. For each combo, upsert into model_capabilities setting last_succeeded_at from most recent successful run, and recent_success_count from story_results joined where status='pass'. This ensures gpt-5.4 shows 535 successful stories immediately on first load — it will never be hidden by a probe that lies. Seed must complete in < 5s. Log a summary: '[model-registry] Seeded N models from codex cache, M from llm-client, K from pipeline history'.

userStories.title: Retrofit pipeline trigger with MODEL_UNAVAILABLE 422 and outcome recording
userStories.description: Two changes to pipeline execution: (1) POST /api/pipeline/trigger calls resolveModel(provider, modelId) before queueing. If the model resolves as unavailable (not null, but computeHealth returns 'unavailable'), return HTTP 422 with body {error: 'Model is unavailable', code: 'MODEL_UNAVAILABLE', requestedModel, suggestedFallback: DEFAULT_MODEL}. If model is unknown (null from resolveModel), allow the run but log a warning — unknown models are given the benefit of the doubt at trigger time. (2) In execution-engine.ts, add recordRunOutcome(provider, modelId, true|false) calls at story end: in the story-pass branch (success=true) and in the story-failed/skipped branch (success=false). Provider is derived from the agent type: agent='codex' → provider='codex', agent='claude' → provider='claude', agent='opencode' → parse from RORCA_MODEL string. This is what keeps real-world success data flowing into the registry.

userStories.title: MCP schema validation at boundary: reject malformed tool calls before they reach routes
userStories.description: Today malformed MCP tool calls reach Express routes and fail with cryptic 500 errors or silent partial failures. Add a validation layer at the MCP HTTP boundary: before forwarding a tool call to the Express route, validate the request body against the route's OpenAPI schema. Use the existing openapi.json (generated by swagger.ts) as the schema source. For each tool call: extract the path + method, find the request body schema in openapi.json, run JSON Schema validation (use ajv, already likely in deps or add it). On validation failure, return a structured MCP error immediately without hitting the route: {error: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', code: 'INVALID_PARAMS', details: [{field, message}]}. This surfaces the problem at the tool-call level — Claude sees a clear error message instead of a 500 or silent partial result. Also validate that required fields are present (specId for enrich, workspaceId for hydrate, etc.).

Validation adds < 5ms overhead per request

userStories.title: Worker health check at MCP boundary and MCP health endpoint
userStories.description: Two operational hardening changes: (1) MCP tool calls that enqueue jobs (generate, enrich, hydrate, batch) must first verify the worker is alive. Check worker_heartbeat table: if last_seen > 90s, return a clear MCP error before enqueueing: {error: 'Worker is not running. Start it with: cd backend && npm run worker', code: 'WORKER_DEAD'}. This prevents silent queuing into a dead queue. (2) Add GET /api/mcp/health endpoint (not behind auth) returning: {status: 'healthy'|'degraded'|'unavailable', worker: {alive, lastSeen, pid}, jobQueue: {queuedCount, runningCount, failedCount}, modelRegistry: {totalModels, healthyModels}, uptime: seconds}. Add this as an MCP tool: rorca_mcp_health — returns the full health payload so Claude can diagnose before taking action. Status is 'degraded' if worker dead, 'unavailable' if DB unreachable.

userStories.title: Idempotency keys: safe retry for all async operations
userStories.description: Extend idempotency (introduced in MR-001's enqueueJob) to all MCP-facing operations. The MCP client wrapper from MR-005 automatically generates an idempotencyKey for each tool call based on {toolName + JSON.stringify(args) + date_hour} — this means retrying the exact same call within the same hour returns the existing jobId, not a new job. Add the idempotencyKey to the MCP tool response: {jobId, idempotencyKey, cached: true|false}. cached=true means the call was deduplicated to an existing job. This protects against Claude retrying a timed-out tool call and creating duplicate specs. Also: add GET /api/jobs?type=spec-generate&idempotencyKey=X endpoint so clients can look up existing jobs by key. On the server side, store idempotencyKey in the pg-boss job data and index it for lookup.
acceptanceCriteria: Calling rorca_specs_generate with identical args twice within 1 hour returns same jobId with cached: true on second call
Calling with different args (different brief text) returns new jobId

userStories.title: Async-aware rorca_specs_generate with built-in polling loop
userStories.description: Add a high-level MCP convenience tool: rorca_generate_and_wait(brief, opts, timeoutSeconds=600). This tool internally calls the async generate endpoint, then polls rorca_job_status every 15 seconds until done or failed or timeoutSeconds exceeded. It streams progress to Claude as intermediate text chunks: 'Generating spec... (pass 1/6: PM Agent)', 'Generating spec... (pass 3/6: UX Designer)', 'Done: 47 stories generated'. If the job succeeds, returns the full spec result. If the job fails, returns the structured error. If timeout exceeded, returns {status: 'still_running', jobId, message: 'Job is still running. Poll rorca_job_status(jobId) to check progress.'}. This tool never times out itself — it always returns within timeoutSeconds with either a result or a still_running status. The key insight: Claude's tool call to rorca_generate_and_wait completes deterministically — worst case it returns 'still running' with the jobId for manual polling.
acceptanceCriteria: rorca_generate_and_wait with a 10-story brief returns the full spec result (status='done') within the polling window

userStories.title: Process supervisor: auto-restart worker on crash with exponential backoff
userStories.description: Today if the worker crashes, pipeline runs silently queue forever. Add a lightweight process supervisor in backend/src/lib/worker-supervisor.ts that: (1) Starts the worker as a child process, (2) Watches for crash (exit code != 0 or SIGKILL), (3) Restarts with exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s... up to max 60s between restarts, (4) Logs each restart with {pid, exitCode, restartCount, nextRestartIn}, (5) After 5 consecutive crashes within 60 seconds, stops auto-restarting and emits a WORKER_CRASH_LOOP alert to the SSE hub (so the UI shows a banner), (6) Exposes isWorkerAlive() and getWorkerStats() for use by the health endpoint in MR-014. The supervisor itself runs as a long-lived process alongside the API server — start it from server.ts if RORCA_PROCESS_ROLE != 'engine'. Worker crash detection uses the worker_heartbeat table as ground truth (heartbeat > 90s = dead, even if process appears running).
acceptanceCriteria: Killing the worker process (kill -9 <pid>) causes it to restart within 2 seconds
After restart, new worker picks up queued jobs successfully

userStories.title: Job result persistence: completed jobs survive backend restarts
userStories.description: Today pg-boss job results are retained for a configurable TTL (default 30 days in pg-boss config). Verify this is set correctly and extend it: completed jobs must be queryable for at least 30 days after completion. Failed jobs must be queryable indefinitely (never auto-purged). Add a separate job_results table: {jobId TEXT PK, type TEXT, status TEXT, result JSONB, error JSONB, createdAt, startedAt, finishedAt, workspaceId, userId, idempotencyKey}. Write-through from completeJob/failJob helpers (MR-001) into this table. The job-queue.ts getJobStatus function reads from job_results first (fast), falls back to pg-boss (slower). This means job status survives even if pg-boss purges completed jobs. Add GET /api/jobs?workspaceId=X&type=spec-generate&limit=50 to list recent jobs by workspace. This lets Claude query 'what specs were generated recently in this workspace' without scanning spec files.

userStories.title: MCP tool: rorca_list_jobs and rorca_cancel_job
userStories.description: Two operational MCP tools: (1) rorca_list_jobs(opts) — lists recent jobs with optional filters: type (spec-generate, enrich, hydrate), status (queued, running, done, failed), workspaceId, limit (default 10). Returns [{jobId, type, status, progress, createdAt, summary}]. Useful for Claude to recover context after session interruption: 'what was I doing?' (2) rorca_cancel_job(jobId) — attempts to cancel a running or queued job. For queued jobs: remove from pg-boss queue (job never starts). For running jobs: send cancel signal to the worker handling that job (worker checks a cancelled flag in job_results before each work unit). For done/failed jobs: return {error: 'Cannot cancel — job already completed', code: 'JOB_ALREADY_DONE'}. Cancel is best-effort for running jobs: if the worker is between work units, it stops; if it's mid-LLM-call, it finishes the current call and stops before the next. This prevents runaway generation jobs consuming quota.

userStories.title: End-to-end integration: 100-story spec via MCP with zero timeouts
userStories.description: Acceptance test story — validate the full MCP reliability stack works end-to-end. Write an automated integration test (backend/tests/mcp-reliability.test.ts using Jest) that: (1) Calls the generate endpoint directly (not via MCP — simulating what the MCP tool does) with a mock brief that produces 100 stories. (2) Receives jobId in < 500ms. (3) Polls getJobStatus every 5s until done or 15min timeout. (4) Verifies result has 100 stories, specId, specPath. (5) Verifies job_results table has the completed job. (6) Calls enrich on the resulting spec, receives jobId in < 200ms, polls until done, verifies all stories enriched. (7) Kills the worker process, calls generate again, verifies WORKER_DEAD error returned. (8) Restarts worker (supervisor auto-starts it), verifies recovery in < 5s. This test is the acceptance gate for the entire Phase 1+2+3 implementation. It must pass in CI before any story in this spec is considered done.
